With h_j=sum_i d(x_i,x_j), the minimum k-subset T contains the k smallest scores and its complement U the k largest; any S has C(S)<=C(U)<=(3-2/k)C(T). A profile of 2k-1 colocated agents and one outlier attains C*/k=1 and ratio (3k-2)/k. For an arbitrary deterministic local rule place its chosen endpoint of one asymmetric pair opposite all other pairs. The quantifiers, repeated indices, zero-optimum inequality and no randomized guarantee were checked. value.rationale: The k-two-agent-group regime is the smallest genuine paired-delegation model in which one must nominate locally before aggregation. Its exact worst-case price is obtained for every deterministic local choice and, more strongly, every k-facility selection, closing the known lower-vs-upper gap within this natural subfamily. This is a motivated sharp uniform metric guarantee rather than rediscovery of the prior lower witness.
